 How is Korean skincare creating a new battleground for beauty advertisers?
 How is Korean skincare creating a new battleground for beauty advertisers?
 As more brands enter the Korean skincare segment, competition for consumer attention and marketplace visibility is likely to increase 
 by
 Imran Fazal
 Published: 
 Nov 7, 2026 8:52 AM 
 | 
 4 min read 
 Follow Us 
 Show Quick Read
 AI-assisted summary, reviewed by our newsroom
 ▼ 
 Korean skincare is gaining mainstream popularity in India's beauty market, with products now representing nearly half of the portfolio managed by digital marketing agency HiveMinds for a leading retailer.
 Changing consumer behavior shows shoppers are increasingly researching brands and products before purchasing, prompting beauty marketers to focus on awareness and education rather than solely on discounts.
 Online beauty retailers are evolving into discovery platforms, allowing brands to reach consumers across various digital touchpoints and emphasizing the need for a full-funnel advertising approach.
 The rise of quick commerce is influencing consumer expectations for faster delivery, making speed a critical factor in online purchase decisions and encouraging beauty brands to align product availability with consumer needs.
 Korean beauty, once a niche segment in India's skincare market, is gaining mainstream traction, prompting beauty brands and retailers to rethink their digital advertising, consumer engagement and marketplace strategies.
 Korean skincare products now account for nearly half the portfolio managed by digital marketing agency HiveMinds for a leading beauty retailer, indicating the growing prominence of the category in online beauty portfolios. The shift also highlights the growing influence of digital platforms in introducing consumers to new products and converting emerging beauty trends into commercial opportunities.

 --> 
 -->
 The development comes amid changing consumer behaviour, with shoppers increasingly researching products and brands before making purchases. For beauty marketers, this means moving beyond discount-led campaigns towards sustained investments in awareness, product education and consideration.
 The 2026 festive sales season reinforced this shift, with HiveMinds observing that consumers were increasingly arriving on marketplaces with their preferred brands and products already shortlisted.
 "The shopper had made up their mind before opening the app: the brand, the product and roughly the price. Discounts brought them in, but no longer decided the purchase," said Vinod M V, SVP - Client Servicing and E-Commerce at HiveMinds.
 He said brands that invested in awareness during September, rather than concentrating their budgets exclusively around the sale period, were better positioned to capture demand.
 Read On: More festive touchpoints, but murkier attribution: Measurement trouble in beauty biz? 
 For Korean skincare brands, this has significant implications. Unlike established beauty categories, emerging product segments require greater consumer education and discovery-led marketing. Brands need to communicate product benefits, build familiarity and establish credibility before shoppers are ready to purchase.
 Discovery becomes a marketing priority 
 The expansion of Korean skincare is also changing the role of online beauty retailers. Marketplaces are increasingly functioning as discovery platforms, introducing shoppers to products and categories beyond their traditional preferences.
 Fashion and lifestyle platforms, too, are expanding into new product categories. HiveMinds observed that a leading oral-care brand built a strong business on a fashion-first platform during the festive season, demonstrating how platforms can use their existing consumer base to create demand for products outside their core categories.
 Read On: Science over stardom? Skincare brands are changing the face of beauty marketing 
 For beauty brands, this opens up opportunities to reach consumers across multiple digital touchpoints rather than relying exclusively on specialist beauty platforms.
 The marketing approach, however, needs to account for a longer consumer journey. Social media content, creator-led communication, product demonstrations and ingredient-focused campaigns can generate initial interest, while search advertising and sponsored marketplace placements can help convert that interest into purchases.
 Competition for digital visibility intensifies 
 As more brands enter the Korean skincare segment, competition for consumer attention and marketplace visibility is likely to increase.
 The festive-season analysis by HiveMinds found that click costs on Flipkart rose to as much as 2.5 times normal levels. Generic searches such as 'trolley bag' lost around half their efficiency, while branded searches remained relatively resilient.
 While these findings relate to the broader e-commerce market, they underline the importance of building brand recognition before major sale events. For beauty advertisers, relying exclusively on generic category keywords and festive discounts could become increasingly expensive.
 Read On: India’s beauty boom moves beyond the D2C playbook 
 "Discovery and conversion are becoming two distinct parts of the beauty shopping journey. Consumers may discover a product through digital content, research it across platforms and eventually purchase it on a marketplace. Marketers need to understand how these touchpoints contribute to the final transaction," said an executive at a beauty retailer, requesting anonymity.
 This could encourage brands to adopt a full-funnel advertising approach, combining awareness campaigns with performance marketing and marketplace investments.
 Quick commerce adds another dimension 
 The growing popularity of quick commerce is adding another layer to the digital beauty retail landscape. Consumers increasingly expect faster fulfilment, and delivery timelines are emerging as an important factor influencing online purchase decisions.
 HiveMinds found that conversion rates in the electronic gadgets category on a leading marketplace declined from 4% to 2% when delivery timelines shifted from next-day delivery to four-seven days.
 "Speed is increasingly becoming a conversion driver, not just a fulfilment advantage," said Aayush Arora, SVP - Revenue & Growth at HiveMinds.
 For beauty companies, this raises the importance of aligning product availability and distribution with different consumer purchase occasions. While traditional marketplaces can cater to planned purchases and wider product discovery, quick commerce could serve immediate replenishment requirements.
 The broader shift is towards treating festive shopping as a consumption window rather than a standalone sales event. For Korean skincare brands, the opportunity will lie in building consumer consideration throughout the year, establishing stronger brand recall and converting growing category interest into repeat purchases.
 For retailers, identifying emerging trends early and turning them into scalable product categories could become an important competitive advantage in India's increasingly crowded online beauty market.
